# Section 3: Basic Eligibility Standard

Section 3 contains three Core Requirements establishing basic eligibility for SACSCOC membership.

## Standard 3.1.a — Degree-Granting Authority [CR] {.core-requirement}

::: {.callout-important}
## Core Requirement
:::

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

The institution has legal authority to grant degrees as demonstrated by authorization from the appropriate governmental agency.

### Typical Evidence Types

- State authorization documents
- Charter or enabling legislation
- NC Community College System authorization
- SBCC approval for programs

### Suggested Owners

- President's Office
- Accreditation Liaison

::: {.callout-note title="NC Considerations"}
NC community colleges receive degree-granting authority through the State Board of Community Colleges (SBCC) and NC General Statutes (Chapter 115D). Include:

- Institutional charter or enabling legislation
- Current State Board authorization
- Relevant NC General Statute citations
:::

---

## Standard 3.1.b — Coursework for Degrees [CR] {.core-requirement}

::: {.callout-important}
## Core Requirement
:::

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

The institution provides instruction for all coursework required for at least one degree program.

### Typical Evidence Types

- Program listings from catalog
- Course schedules showing offerings
- Documentation of courses taught by the institution

### Suggested Owners

- VP Academic Affairs
- Registrar

### Common Pitfalls / Weak Evidence

- Cannot clearly demonstrate that core coursework is offered
- Consortium or contractual arrangements unclear

---

## Standard 3.1.c — Continuous Operation [CR] {.core-requirement}

::: {.callout-important}
## Core Requirement
:::

### What SACSCOC is Trying to Ensure

The institution is in operation and has students enrolled in its degree programs.

### Typical Evidence Types

- Enrollment data (historical and current)
- Graduation/completion data
- Institutional Summary Form

### Suggested Owners

- Institutional Research/Effectiveness
- Registrar

### Common Pitfalls / Weak Evidence

- Data gaps or inconsistencies in enrollment reporting
- Unable to demonstrate continuous operation
